analysis.title: US TMT what a week (Peter Callahan, 8 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX fell about 5% last week and is on a 4-week losing streak. The SOX fell 28% over 22 days, one of the largest rolling 1-month drawdowns in history.
Earnings were secondary last week. Attention went to risk reduction and re-calibrating datacenter build expectations after last Tuesday's mid-term election.

Flow signals were extreme: record put volumes, elevated ETF volumes, panic readings in vol metrics, elevated sell skews and oversold conditions. The author says this arguably sets up technical relief once vol normalizes and risk appetite rebases.

By the end of the week, investor conversations moved to what is priced in for y/y capex (or GW) builds over the next few years, and whether too much of a 2028+ slowdown is already priced. The author calls this more of a 2028+ exercise than a 2027 one.

Sentiment is described as very tough. Bottoms-up data (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings) is strong, while AI/Semis have been in a rolling bear market since summer and are about 40% off the highs.

Under the surface there was some progress over the last month: strong earnings, oil and rates relief, lowered expectations, and positioning and valuation resets. Portfolio managers still face tension. The short leg of a semis L/S book is hard to run when everything is compressed, and diversifying is hard because many areas outside Semis/Tech have re-rated.
DRAM names (MU, Hynix, Samsung) trade at 2-3x forward P/E while spot DRAM prices remain near highs. Investors are debating whether those multiples are interesting or risky.
Analog semis were relatively resilient until late last week, even as industrial names saw outflows and drawdowns (CAT vs TXN charted).
The valuation premium of S&P staples to the SPX is at its highest in 10+ years. The consumer staples index trades at about 2x the 24-month forward multiple of the semiconductor index.
Info Tech again paced the market higher with best-in-class 3Q earnings results, even though the screens do not show it.

This week has lighter earnings (AMAT, CSCO, TTWO, IFX, SE) plus analyst days and macro data (CPI, PPI). The author expects a 'day at a time' market with less benefit of the doubt for bull-case frameworks.

Top client questions: what inning of the AI cycle, whether there is a turn before year-end, which non-AI names are durable (ABNB, FWONK, SPHR, LYV, TTWO, DIS), views on software high-flyers (NET, DDOG), semis preferences after the drawdown, whether moves in APP and U are real, online travel agency preference into 2027 (BKNG/EXPE vs ABNB), and what to do with Memory.

sector_views.rationale: Deep drawdown with washed-out flows and positioning could allow technical relief, but investors face two-way data and unresolved debate over 2028+ datacenter build.
The author flags that staples' valuation premium to the SPX is at a 10+ year high, so names up 'too much' may draw attention, without making an explicit call.

Earnings this week (no estimates given): Mon post-market includes TTWO, TTD, RKLB, ONTO, PLUG. Tue pre-market includes SE, IFX, SoftBank, WIX, with post-market CRWV, RGTI. Thu pre-market NBIS, with post-market AMAT, CSCO, NU.

tension_points.bull_case: Bottoms-up data remains strong (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings), and record put volumes, panic vol readings and oversold conditions set up technical relief.
tension_points.bear_case: Price action is demanding linearity, with Semis about 40% off the highs, policy and datacenter construction debates unresolved, and further choppy two-way datapoints expected.
